explain.say: Imagine building a mountain out of stone blocks, each as heavy as two cars, with no machines at all! About 4,500 years ago, Egyptians did just that. Look at the chain: these are the steps for building the Great Pyramid of King Khufu.

explain.say: By boat! Look at the boat box. Huge granite blocks came about 800 kilometres down the River Nile from Aswan. A papyrus diary from a man called Merer even describes shipping stone by boat. Then they dragged blocks on wooden sledges. Can you see the water drop?

faq.q: How did they move the huge stones?
faq.a: By boat along the Nile and canals, then on wooden sledges pulled by teams of workers over sand made wet to lower friction, and up ramps.
asks: How did the Egyptians lift the blocks?

faq.a: Paid workers, not slaves. Archaeologists found their village, bakeries and tombs near the pyramids. Many farmers worked there when the Nile flood covered their fields.

faq.q: How long did it take to build the Great Pyramid?
faq.a: About 20 years, finished around 2560 BCE for King Khufu.
asks: When was the Great Pyramid built?

faq.q: How tall is the Great Pyramid?
faq.a: It was about 146 metres tall when built. Its top stones are gone, so it is about 138 metres today.
asks: How big is the Great Pyramid?

faq.q: Why does wet sand help pull a sledge?
faq.a: Water sticks the sand grains together, so the sand stays firm instead of piling up in front of the sledge. Scientists found it can halve the pulling force.
asks: Why did Egyptians pour water on sand?

facts: The Great Pyramid of Khufu was completed around 2560 BCE and was originally about 146 metres tall.
It is made of about 2.3 million stone blocks.
Papyri found at Wadi al-Jarf record an official named Merer shipping limestone for the Great Pyramid.
